newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Down on selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Down on selling pressure.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices fell, buckling under pressure in a well-offered market as buyers stayed at the sidelines, traders said on Monday.
Late Asian trading day, at least two offers emerged for 180-cst supplies and one for a 380-cst cargo for loading in July.
Traders said the prompt market is weak as reflected in a narrower inter-month spread. July/August spread fell by a marginal 25 cents a barrel late Monday.
Traders said stocks in Singapore are still high and supplies are more than adequate to meet demand.
"There are more prompt cargoes on offer and demand would only pick up later," said one trader.
Thailand has issued a tender to buy 80,000 tonnes of fuel oil for August 15-25 delivery to Sri Racha.
The tender seeks 75,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade, 2.0-percent sulphur and 5,000 tonnes of 180-cst, 1.0-percent fuel oil. The tender closes July 1 and offers would be valid until July 2.
PTT has has issued the tender as its term contracts could not satisfy demand, traders said.
PTT sources did not say if the company will continue to issue spot tenders in additional to its term imports.
Traders also expected Chinese demand to pick up in August after the handover.
Swaps prices were steady. July was quoted at $98.25/$99.00 and August at $98.00/$98.75, little changed from last Friday.
